mainTopic: When does a נזיר who became טמא start his new count of נזירות טהרה: the seventh day, the eighth day, or after his חטאת and אשם are brought?
overview: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from the extra words "ביום ההוא" that the new נזירות starts on the seventh day. רבי uses the same words for something else: the count starts on the eighth day even before the קרבנות are brought. The גמרא then asks why רב חסדא did not explain the משנה according to רבי, using impurity on the night before the eighth day. רב אדא בר אהבה explains that for רבי, the new נזירות begins exactly when the קרבן can be brought, so the night case never fits the משנה. Next the גמרא quotes a ברייתא with three views on when the new count begins. רבי אליעזר says on the eighth day itself. חכמים say after the חטאת. רבי ישמעאל says only after both the חטאת and the אשם. Each view's reading of the word "ההוא" is explained, including a debate over whether the עולה, which is only a gift, needs a word at all. Finally the גמרא begins a ברייתא giving the רבנן's source, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The source for starting on the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: The words "ביום ההוא" are extra for the eighth day, so רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה applies them to the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the פסוק need to say "on that day"? If it is not needed for the eighth day, apply it to the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gets his view that the new נזירות starts on the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is already talking about the eighth day, so the words "on that day" are not needed there. Since they add nothing about the eighth day, they are moved to the seventh day. That is the day he becomes טהור and shaves.

keyTerms.meaning: "on that day": the words being explained
"if it is not needed for this matter": a way of moving an extra word to a different topic
"apply it to another matter"

phrases.english: Why do I need "on that day"?
If it is not needed for the eighth day,
apply it to the seventh day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אם אינו ענין לשמיני תנהו ענין לשביעי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, which was discussed before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra words "ביום ההוא" teach that the new נזירות begins on the seventh day.

steps.title: What does רבי do with "on that day"?
steps.stepSummary: רבי also has the words "ביום ההוא" in the פסוק, so what does he learn from them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי too, isn't it written "on that day"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי: the same extra words are in the פסוק for him too, so they must teach him something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds the new count begins on the eighth day. If the words are extra, it looks like they should push the start to the seventh day, as רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says. The גמרא wants to know how רבי uses them.

keyTerms.meaning: "but isn't it written"

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi too,
isn't it written "on that day"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the source from step 1 against the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that the new נזירות starts on the eighth day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words are in the פסוק for רבי too, so he must either learn the seventh day from them or give them another use.

steps.title: The count starts even before the קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: רבי uses the words to teach that the new count begins on the eighth day itself, even if he has not yet brought his קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי would say: that phrase comes to teach that even if he did not bring his קרבנות, his count still starts on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי by giving the words a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, "ביום ההוא" ties the start of the new נזירות to the day itself, not to bringing the קרבנות. So even a נזיר who delays his קרבנות starts counting on the eighth day.

keyTerms.meaning: "it comes for this purpose"
his קרבנות (the offerings brought after becoming טהור)

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions learn from "ביום ההוא". רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns that the count starts on the seventh day. רבי learns that it starts on the eighth day even without the קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rabbi would say to you:
that phrase comes for this purpose —
to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: even though he did not bring his offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר לך רבי ההוא להכי הוא דאתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra words a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words should move the start of the count to the seventh day.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, the words teach that the eighth day starts the count even without the קרבנות.

steps.title: Why not explain the משנה according to רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא needed רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He could have explained the משנה according to רבי, with impurity on the night before the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What forced רב חסדא to say the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה? Let him say it is a case where he became טמא on the night of the eighth day, and then it follows רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: there seems to be an easier way to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a נזיר who became טמא many times brings only one set of קרבנות. רב חסדא said this only works according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. But according to רבי, if each impurity happened at night, the new נזירות had already started, and he still could not have brought קרבנות at night. So the משנה could fit רבי too.

keyTerms.meaning: "what forced him?"
to explain the case or the opinion behind it
the night before the eighth day

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda, what forced him
to say it follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?
Let him explain it as a case where he became impure,
where he "saw" impurity on the night of the eighth,
phrases.notes: "Saw" here means he came into contact with טומאה.

phrases.english: and then it follows Rabbi!

steps.triggerLanguage: ורב חסדא מאי דוחקיה לאוקמיה כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי's view is clear, the גמרא asks whether the משנה could follow him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the משנה follows only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A case of impurity at night seems to make the משנה fit רבי too, so there was no need to limit it.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא hold night is not too early?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב חסדא did not use the night case because he holds that night is not מחוסר זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he did not explain it according to רבי, shall we say he holds that night is not "lacking time"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to learn something about רב חסדא's opinion from the fact that he did not use the easier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If night is not מחוסר זמן, then night counts as if he could already bring his קרבנות. Impurity that night would then need a second set, and the night case would not fit the משנה. That would explain why רב חסדא avoided it.

keyTerms.meaning: "shall we say?": suggests a conclusion
"he holds"
"lacking time": too early to bring the קרבן

phrases.english: Since he did not explain it according to Rabbi,
shall we say he holds
that night is not "lacking time"?
phrases.notes: קרבנות can't be brought at night. The question is whether night still counts as part of his time to bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מדלא מוקים לה כרבי לימא קסבר ליליא לאו מחוסר זמן הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חסדא's silence about the night case to guess his view on night.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב חסדא hold that night is not מחוסר זמן?

steps.title: The two go together, so nothing can be proven
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the start of the new נזירות depends on when the קרבן can be brought. So the night case fails for רבי either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: one depends on the other. If night is too early, he can bring the קרבן only in the morning, so the new נזירות also starts only in the morning. If night is not too early, the new נזירות starts in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה rejects the proof from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the new נזירות starts exactly when the קרבן can be brought. If night is too early, the new נזירות has not started yet, so impurity at night is not a case of becoming טמא during a new נזירות at all. If night is not too early, the new נזירות has started and he could already bring his קרבנות, so he needs a second set. Either way the night case cannot explain the משנה, so we learn nothing about רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: "this depends on that"
morning
evening
the new, pure נזירות he counts after becoming טהור
takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, the new נזירות begins exactly when the נזיר can bring his קרבן. So whatever one holds about night, the night case cannot fit the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a proof from "he didn't say this other answer" fails when the other answer was never possible anyway.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
This depends on that.
If you say night is "lacking time,"
when is he fit for the offering? In the morning,

phrases.aramaic: נְזִירוּת נָמֵי לָא חָיְילָא עַד צַפְרָא.
phrases.english: so the nezirus also does not take effect until the morning.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ לֵילְיָא אֵינוֹ מְחוּסַּר זְמַן —
phrases.english: And if you say night is not "lacking time" —
the nezirus of purity takes effect from the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אדא בר אהבה הא בהא תליא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof about רב חסדא's view on night, and also answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The night case never works for רבי, because the new נזירות and the time to bring the קרבן always start together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Nothing can be learned about רב חסדא's view on night. He used רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה because the משנה cannot follow רבי.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the eighth day starts a new count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that becoming טמא again on the seventh day means only one set of קרבנות. Becoming טמא on each eighth day means a set of קרבנות for each time. רבי אליעזר says the new count starts right away on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: If he became impure on the seventh day, and again became impure on the seventh day, he brings only one set of offerings. If he became impure on the eighth day, and again became impure on the eighth day, he brings a set of offerings for each time. He begins counting right away. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a ברייתא about a נזיר who keeps becoming טמא while he is finishing his purification. This first part gives רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the seventh day he is still in the middle of his טומאה, so a new טומאה just joins the old one. One set of קרבנות covers both. By the eighth day, רבי אליעזר holds that a new נזירות has already begun, even before his קרבנות are brought. So each new טומאה counts as a separate event with its own קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא is now quoting in full a source it mentioned earlier
The seventh day of his purification from טומאת מת
The eighth day, when the נזיר brings his קרבנות
He begins counting his new, pure days of נזירות

phrases.english: The matter itself: If he became impure on the seventh day,
phrases.notes: He was already טמא once and is now on day seven of his purification when a new טומאה happens.

phrases.english: and again became impure on the seventh day,
he brings only one set of offerings.
If he became impure on the eighth day, and again became impure on the eighth day,

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: he brings a set of offerings for each and every one.
He begins counting right away,
phrases.notes: 'Right away' means from the eighth day itself, even if he has not yet brought his קרבנות.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא behind the eighth-day discussion in the earlier steps
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: the eighth day itself starts a new נזירות, even before the קרבנות are brought. So each טומאה on an eighth day needs its own קרבנות.

steps.title: חכמים: the new count waits for the sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say all the times he became טמא count as one, needing one set of קרבנות, until he brings his חטאת. Once the חטאת is brought, even without the אשם, he starts counting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: one set of offerings for all of them, until he brings his חטאת. If he brought his חטאת and became impure, and brought his חטאת and became impure, he brings a set of offerings for each one. If he brought his חטאת but not his אשם, he counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the view of חכמים, who disagree with רבי אליעזר about when the new count begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the eighth day alone does not start a new נזירות. Bringing the חטאת is what starts it. Before that, every new טומאה joins the old one. After the חטאת, the count starts even if the אשם has not been brought yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering, one of the קרבנות a טמא נזיר brings
Guilt-offering, also brought by a טמא נזיר
One set of offerings covers all the times he became טמא

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
one set of offerings for all of them,
until he brings his sin-offering.
If he brought his sin-offering and became impure,
and brought his sin-offering and became impure again,

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: he brings a set of offerings for each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיא חַטָּאתוֹ וְלֹא הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ — מוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: If he brought his sin-offering but not his guilt-offering, he counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: the new נזירות begins only after the חטאת is brought. The אשם does not hold it back.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the guilt-offering also holds him back
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the אשם holds back the new count just like the חטאת does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: Just as his חטאת held him back, so his אשם holds him back.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא goes one step further than חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the new count waits until both the חטאת and the אשם are brought. If he becomes טמא before the אשם is brought, all of it is still one long טומאה with one set of קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back or prevents: here, from starting the new count
'Just as... so too': a comparison that gives both cases the same rule

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on when the new count starts. רבי אליעזר: on the eighth day itself. חכמים: after the חטאת. רבי ישמעאל: after both the חטאת and the אשם.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
Just as his sin-offering held him back,
phrases.notes: He is pointing to חכמים, who agreed that not yet bringing the חטאת keeps him from starting the count.

phrases.english: so his guilt-offering holds him back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the view of חכמים and goes further
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the חטאת and the אשם must be brought before the new נזירות begins.

steps.title: Where רבי אליעזר and the רבנן learn their views in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר learns from 'ביום ההוא' that the count starts even before any קרבנות. The רבנן learn from 'ההוא' that it starts even without the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well for רבי אליעזר: the פסוק says 'And he shall sanctify his head on that day', even though he has not brought his קרבנות. And the רבנן: 'that' teaches even though he has not brought his אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the first two opinions fit the פסוק. The word בשלמא tells us it is setting up a question about רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן use the extra word 'ההוא' to teach that something missing does not hold back the count. For רבי אליעזר, that is all the קרבנות. For the רבנן, it is only the אשם. The question waiting next is what רבי ישמעאל, who holds that even the אשם holds him back, learns from 'ההוא'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works out well for...': sets up a coming question on a different opinion
'And he shall sanctify his head': the restart of his נזירות

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא means 'this view works,' and it is setting up a challenge. The challenge about the remaining opinion, רבי ישמעאל, comes in the next step.

phrases.english: It works out well for Rabbi Eliezer,
the verse says:
'And he shall sanctify his head on that day',

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: even though he has not brought his offerings.
And the Rabbis: 'that' day teaches,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: even though he has not brought his guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the source in the פסוק for the first two opinions and prepares a question on the third
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ביום ההוא' shows that some missing קרבנות do not hold back the count. For רבי אליעזר that means all of them; for the רבנן, only the אשם.

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל learn from the word 'that'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל needs the word 'ההוא' if, for him, the אשם also holds back the new count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי ישמעאל, why do I need the word 'that'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל and asks what the word 'ההוא' teaches him. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, the רבנן used 'ההוא' to teach that the count starts even without the אשם. רבי ישמעאל says the אשם does hold back the count, so it seems the word has no job in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (What does this word teach?)
'That', from the words 'on that day'

phrases.english: But according to רבי ישמעאל,
why do I need the word 'that'?
phrases.notes: This is the word 'ההוא' from 'ביום ההוא', במדבר 6:11, which the רבנן used in step 10.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source reading from step 10 to רבי ישמעאל's view and asks what the word does for him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי ישמעאל learns from 'ההוא', since he holds that the אשם does hold back the count.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that the אשם also holds back the new count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under בשלמא, 'ההוא' explains the views of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן. If the אשם also holds back the count, the word seems to have nothing left to teach רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: 'That' teaches the burnt-offering does not hold back the count
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses 'ההוא' to teach that the count starts even if the עולה was not brought yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: 'That' teaches that he starts counting even though he has not brought his burnt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי ישמעאל. He uses the word to teach that the עולה does not hold back the new count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same word but apply it to different offerings. For the רבנן it removes the אשם. For רבי ישמעאל it only removes the עולה, so the אשם still holds back the count.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (the גמרא answers on his behalf)
Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Even though he did not

phrases.english: He could say to you:
'That' teaches: even though
he has not brought his burnt-offering, he starts counting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: ״הַהוּא״ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא עוֹלָתוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי ישמעאל, 'ההוא' teaches that the count can start before the עולה is brought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the אשם holds back the count for רבי ישמעאל, 'ההוא' seems to teach him nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, 'ההוא' teaches that the עולה does not hold back the count.

steps.title: The רבנן: a burnt-offering is only a gift and needs no special word
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say no word is needed to teach that the עולה does not hold back the count, because it is only a gift. So 'ההוא' is free to teach about the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: a burnt-offering does not need a word to limit it, because it is only a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not read the word the way רבי ישמעאל does. For them, the עולה never needed a word in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is a gift to ה׳ and is not part of the נזיר's כפרה, so it obviously does not hold back his new count. That means 'ההוא' must teach something new, and the רבנן say it teaches that even the אשם does not hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: A limiting word in the פסוק that excludes something
A gift
Merely, just

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read 'ההוא'. רבי ישמעאל: it removes only the עולה. The רבנן: the עולה is just a gift and needs no word, so the word removes the אשם.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis respond:
A burnt-offering does not need a limiting word,
since it is merely a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reason for not reading 'ההוא' the way רבי ישמעאל reads it in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using 'ההוא' only for the עולה. It does not reject רבי ישמעאל's conclusion inside his own view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A gift-offering obviously does not hold back the count, so a word in the פסוק would not be spent teaching that.

steps.title: What is the source of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the רבנן's reason that only the חטאת holds back the new count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the רבנן's source. It sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said in step 8 that once the חטאת is brought, the count starts even without the אשם. The גמרא now wants a clear source showing that the אשם does not hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their reason?
The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the word 'ההוא' to a fuller source for the רבנן's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the אשם does not hold back the start of the new נזירות.

steps.title: A ברייתא raises the idea that the guilt-offering holds back the count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the נזיר's אשם and suggests that, like every other אשם, it might hold him back. It is about to reject this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: 'And he shall consecrate to ה׳ the days of his נזירות, and he shall bring a lamb in its first year for an אשם.' What does this come to teach? Since we find that every אשם in the תורה holds things back, one might think this one also holds him back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that supports the רבנן. Here the ברייתא only lays out the possible mistaken idea, and its answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other אשם in the תורה is needed before the person is fully done, so we might guess the נזיר's אשם works the same way and stops his new count. The word 'יכול' marks this as a guess the ברייתא is going to knock down.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall consecrate (start his נזירות again)
Guilt-offering
What does the פסוק come to teach?
Hold back, are required before something can happen
One might think (an idea about to be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא has not finished. The idea that the אשם holds him back is only a 'יכול', and it is not the ruling of the רבנן.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'And he shall consecrate to the Lord the days of his naziriteship,'
'and he shall bring a lamb in its first year for a guilt-offering.'
What does this come to teach?
phrases.notes: Notice that the פסוק puts starting the days before bringing the אשם. That order is what the ברייתא is asking about.

phrases.english: Since we have found that all guilt-offerings
in the Torah hold things back,
one might think this one also holds him back.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְהִזִּיר לַה׳ אֶת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ וְהֵבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ לְאָשָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts giving the source asked for in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that the אשם does not hold back the start of the new count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on במדבר 6:12, which puts starting the days before bringing the אשם. So far it has only raised the opposing 'יכול'.
